prompt: Fill in a JTabbedPane-backed note pad: addNote(title, body) creates a tab holding a JTextArea, plus tabCount(), titleAt(i), and bodyAt(i). Complete the starter file, then run the tests.
explanation: A JTabbedPane is a container whose children are whole components, so addTab(title, component) stores the title and the page together and getComponentAt(index) hands the component back as a plain java.awt.Component. That is why bodyAt has to cast to JTextArea before it can call getText() -- and why wrapping the area in a JScrollPane would change what getComponentAt returns. Guarding the index yourself and returning null keeps the accessors from throwing IndexOutOfBoundsException when a caller asks for a tab that does not exist.
hints: addNote builds the page component first -- a JTextArea holding the body text -- then hands it to the tabbed pane's addTab along with the title.
tabCount() and titleAt() delegate straight to getTabCount() and getTitleAt(index).
Both accessors need the same guard -- return null when index is negative or not less than getTabCount() -- before touching the pane.
